title: The PERFECT Hybrid Calisthenics Program (Feat Bald Omni Man)
summary: NH presents a 4-day upper/lower/push/pull hybrid program, built with Bald Omni Man, that uses calisthenics compounds for the bulk of upper-body work and free weights for isolation and legs. Every superset is a bi-set, with free-weight swaps for each calisthenics lift. The program hammers the upper back while keeping lower-back fatigue in check, and it targets intermediates.
claims: NH got sick for the first time in 15 years and chose training and recovery over making videos
Calisthenics lacks isolation, so lagging muscles like triceps are hard to bring up; use calisthenics compounds for bulk work and free weights to finish
Calisthenics alone cannot build legs as big as free weights can
If your goal is hypertrophy and you are not supersetting, you are leaving gains on the table; this program uses only two-exercise bi-sets
NH and Bald Omni Man share the exercise selection and frequency but differ in volume and intensity; NH's split is upper, lower, push, pull
Schedule: Mon upper, Wed lower, Fri push, Sat pull; rest days follow upper and lower because they carry the most work
Weighted push-ups are easier to recover from than weighted dips because of the shorter range, so they get more volume: push-ups 3-6x10-15, dips 3-4x6-10
Six or seven sets of weighted dips would be junk volume
The rep range should align with the number of sets you can do
Calisthenics trains grip but lacks elbow and wrist flexion work for forearms; reverse curls (3-6x8-15) fill the gap
Ring rows to failure, or barbell/seal rows 4x8-12, superset with EZ curls 4x6-10 or cable curls 4x10-15
NH has fallen in love with decline ring push-ups and favors them over regular ring push-ups for upper chest and shoulders
Lying triceps extensions (4x10-12) are essential in a hybrid program because calisthenics neglects the long head
Heel-elevated squats (3-5x6-12) or hack squats (3-5x8-15) give nearly pure quad work while sparing the posterior chain
Calisthenics athletes tend to have small necks; do neck extensions and flexions superset with heavy lower-body work
Weighted chin-ups 3-5x4-10: never under 4 reps; any added weight that challenges you counts
You must isolate the abs to maximize their hypertrophy: hanging knee raises to failure or weighted decline sit-ups 12-20
Calisthenics athletes have massive upper backs because they train them every session; the program copies this while controlling lower-back fatigue
Block pulls can add upper-trap work, which calisthenics neglects
Calf raises are included because chicken legs run in the family in calisthenics
This is an intermediate program for people already adept at both free weights and calisthenics; novices should use his novice programs
Handstand push-ups must use a deficit; the limit should be hands reaching the upper chest, never the head touching down
Bodyweight sets to failure might go 20, 18, 16, 14, 12 for someone very good at handstand push-ups
Use isolation to fix arms lagging behind push-up-built chest and delts, but do not swing to massive arms on a small torso
Keep upright rows and lateral raises at 12-15 reps, no lower, to keep shoulders safe
Since the upper back is trained every session, check recovery: pick ring rows instead of dumbbell rows on Friday if needed
RDLs 4x8-12 or stiff-legged deadlifts 4x6-10 open the pull day
A few very intense heavy lower-body sets are enough; with this much upper-back work you could not recover from 8 squat sets plus deadlifts 3x/week anyway
A six-pack needs ab training with stretch and contraction, not just getting lean
Close-grip neutral lat pulldowns are inferior to pull-ups; the pull-up stretch is unmatched
The program gives about 9 hard quad sets and 8 hard posterior-chain sets per week, which is enough
exercises: main upper compound, easier recovery than dips
more stimulus and fatigue, so fewer sets
upper chest and shoulders vs chest
